Reasoning: Let the acute angle at each A vertex be α, and let the acute angle marked at each B notch be β. Since B is a concave vertex, its actual interior angle as a simple closed polygon is not β, but 360° − β; the actual interior angle at an A vertex is α. This star shape has 2n vertices in total, so the sum of its interior angles is (2n − 2)180°. Therefore nα + n(360° − β) = (2n − 2)180°. Simplifying: nα + 360n − nβ = 360n − 360, so n(β − α) = 360. The problem states that the acute angle at A_1 is 10° smaller than the acute angle at B_1, that is, β − α = 10°, so n = 360/10 = 36.

Because B is a reentrant notch in the simple closed polygon, the actual interior angle at each B vertex is 360° − β, while the actual interior angle at each A vertex is α. Use the interior-angle sum for a 2n-gon: nα + n(360° − β) = (2n − 2)180°. This simplifies to n(β − α) = 360°. The text says α is 10° less than β, so β − α = 10°, giving n = 360/10 = 36.

method.method_draft: From the diagram, traverse the boundary of the star through alternating outer points A_i and inner notches B_i. Let α be the acute angle at an A point and β be the acute angle at a B notch. At an outer A vertex, the direction of travel makes a left turn of 180° − α. At an inward B notch, the turn is in the opposite direction with signed turn β − 180°, because the polygon interior there is reflex. Thus each A-to-B-to-next-A pair contributes a net signed turn of (180° − α) + (β − 180°) = β − α. There are n identical pairs around the simple closed star, so the total signed turn is 360°: n(β − α) = 360°. Since the text gives β − α = 10°, n = 36.
